assertions.notes: Recommends form.WithAccessible(true), describing it as replacing the full-screen UI with plain line-by-line prompts.
Advises against screen-reader detection and offers a flag, an environment variable, and a saved config setting.
Explains that NVDA diffs the screen on each redraw, so arrow-key moves re-read the menu, and that appended text reads well.
States that Bubble Tea and Bubbles have nothing built in for screen readers, so the rest of the app needs its own linear mode.
Recommends a flag for every onboarding question (--name, --region, --no-telemetry) so setup can run with no prompts.
The answer recommends `form.WithAccessible(true).Run()`, which asks one plain question per line with numbered selects and no redraws.
The answer recommends a `--accessible` flag, an env var, and a saved config key, and says explicitly not to try detecting a screen reader.
The answer explains that each keypress redraws the screen and that moving the Select highlight is read out again by NVDA, so linear prompts avoid this.
The answer says Bubble Tea and Bubbles have no screen-reader support and lays out linear-mode rules for the rest of the app.
Step 3 says to give every onboarding answer a flag or config equivalent so the prompts can be skipped entirely.
Recommends form.WithAccessible(true), describing it as dropping Bubble Tea and asking each field as a plain prompt one line at a time.
Offers an --accessible flag, a MYAPP_ACCESSIBLE env var and a saved config key, and states that screen readers can't be reliably detected, so users must opt in.
Explains that NVDA diffs the screen and the full-screen redraw on each keypress re-reads the menu and announces focus changes and borders as new text.
States that Bubble Tea and Bubbles have no screen-reader support and describes a linear runPlain mode for the rest of the app.
Recommends a flag for every onboarding question (myapp init --name … --region …) so setup can run with no prompts at all.
Section 3 says every TUI action must be reachable through subcommands, flags, or a numbered menu, and that nothing should be TUI-only.
It shows labelled records such as 'Service: api' and 'Status: degraded', and offers --format text|csv|json.
Section 5 sends results to stdout and prompts, progress, and diagnostics to stderr.
It forbids spinners and progress bars, uses occasional lines like 'Checked 3 of 10 services', and ends with a 'Done.' status line.
It uses words for status instead of colors, glyphs, or column position, and drops borders, separators, and ASCII art.
Section 6 offers a DASH_PLAIN environment variable and a 'plain = true' config key so the mode stays enabled.
Includes a section and table mapping each TUI interaction (restart, confirm modal, picker, filter, detail pane) to a plain-mode command.
Outputs Header: value blocks and also offers --format json|csv as a separate option.
States the stream contract explicitly: results on stdout, prompts and progress on stderr.
Watch mode prints a line only when state changes, ends with a status line, and forbids spinners, using a single 'Fetching metrics…' line instead.
Every value is labelled so meaning doesn't depend on column position, color, or glyphs; box drawing is removed and no color is emitted.
Adds the DASH_PLAIN env var and a config key so the user sets it once.
Says every TUI action should exist as a subcommand or flag, gives restart/ack/show examples, and adds a coverage test over the action enum.
Uses labelled 'Field: value' lines and offers --format text|csv|json|ndjson.
Says results go to stdout and progress goes to stderr as one static line.
Ends with a final 'Done.' status line, uses a static progress line on stderr, and forbids spinners and timed full reprints.
States are words rather than colored dots, charts become sentences, and there is no block or box-drawing characters; it also explains why columns fail.
Accepts the MYAPP_PLAIN env var and a ui.mode config key so the mode doesn't need passing each time.
The answer says no and explains that the browser client is xterm.js drawing the grid onto a canvas with screen-reader mode off, so a screen reader has nothing to navigate.
The answer states Textual has no screen-reader support, no accessibility tree and no widget roles, and that the roadmap item is still open.
The answer recommends a linear plain mode alongside the TUI, enabled by a --plain flag or environment variable, with concrete guidance.
The answer says no and explains that the browser client draws the grid with xterm.js on a canvas with xterm's screen-reader mode off, so screen readers gain nothing.
The answer states that Textual itself has no screen-reader support and that the roadmap item is still open.
The answer recommends shipping a linear plain mode (--no-tui or an env var) and gives detailed guidance for it.
The answer opens with 'No' and explains that the browser client uses xterm.js to draw onto a canvas with screen-reader mode off, so the screen reader only gets a picture of a terminal.
The answer says Textual has no screen-reader support of its own and that the item is still open on its roadmap.
The answer recommends a linear plain mode (e.g. --plain) as part of the product, with detailed rules for how it should behave.
The answer says the env var only changes formatting to plain linear text, and Ink still erases and rewrites everything outside <Static> on every state change.
It moves completed messages into <Static> so they print once, and limits the SR-mode live region to the input line plus one status line.
It replaces the spinner with a static 'Working…' line and says to stop elapsed-time counters and other per-tick timers.
aria-label appears only to describe what Ink does in SR mode; the answer never recommends aria-label or aria-hidden for visual-only elements and instead removes or conditionally renders them.
It says nothing in Ink detects a screen reader, and recommends a --screen-reader flag and a saved config setting instead of trying to detect NVDA.
The answer says the screen-reader renderer prints flat text but still erases and rewrites the whole live (non-Static) region on every state change.
Step 1 moves finished messages into append-only <Static>, and step 2 limits the live region to the prompt plus at most one status line.
Step 3 replaces the spinner with a static 'Assistant is responding…' line and removes ticking timers and counters.
Step 5 puts aria-hidden on decorative glyphs and aria-label on meaningful icons.
The answer states Ink never detects a screen reader and recommends documenting the env var or a --screen-reader flag, saved as a setting.
The answer says screen-reader mode prints linear text but still erases and rewrites the whole live region on every change; the flag changes what is drawn, not how often.
It moves finished messages into <Static> so they print once, and keeps the live region to about one line (prompt plus at most one status line).
It replaces the spinner with a single 'Assistant is thinking…' line and drops per-second timers and token meters in screen-reader mode.
aria-label is mentioned only as part of how Ink's mode behaves; the answer never recommends adding aria-label or aria-hidden to visual-only elements and instead says to remove them.
It states that nothing detects a screen reader, that useIsScreenReaderEnabled only reports the flag, and recommends a --screen-reader flag or saved setting.
